## FINANCES AND BUDGET (continued)

| Item | DIY Estimate | Movers Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contingency fund | 10–15% of total | same | Recommended cushion for surprises |
| Cleaning (old place, for deposit) | $150–$400 | same | DIY vs. professional |
| Tips for movers | n/a | $100–$300 | ~$20–$40 per mover per day |
| Mail forwarding (USPS) | $1.10 | same | Identity verification fee |
| New home basics (shower curtain, trash cans, etc.) | $200–$500 | same | You'll be surprised what you need day one |

**Rough all-in totals:**
- **DIY (truck + drive both):** $4,000–$8,000
- **Hybrid (container + drive car):** $5,000–$9,000
- **Full-service movers + ship one car + drive other:** $8,000–$14,000+
- **Full-service movers + ship both cars + fly:** $10,000–$16,000+

Add deposits, first month's rent, and temporary housing on top — easily another $3,000–$6,000.

*Print this, fold it, keep it in the glove box.*

**MOVING DAY ESSENTIALS — KEEP WITH YOU**

**Documents Pouch (in the car, never in the truck):**
- Driver's licenses, passports
- Vehicle titles, registration, insurance cards
- Lease/closing papers (both homes)
- Moving contract + Bill of Lading + inventory
- Dog records: rabies cert, vaccines, microchip #, vet contact
- Prescriptions + medication list

- Bank/credit card contact numbers
- Cash ($200–$400) + checkbook

**Tech Kit:**
- Phones + chargers (car + wall)

- Laptop + charger
- USB drive with photo backup of valuables
- Headphones, dash mount, car charger

**Day-of Comfort Bag (per person):**
- 2–3 days of clothes + pajamas
- Toiletries, toothbrush, meds
- Water bottle, snacks
- Pillow + light blanket
- Sunglasses, hat

**Dog Go-Bag:**
- 7+ days of food in a sealed container
- Water + collapsible bowl
- Leash + backup leash
- Current ID tag with new phone #
- Crate or car harness/barrier
- Poop bags
- Medications + vet records copy
- Familiar blanket + favorite toy

**Tool & Fix-It Kit:**
- Basic screwdriver set + pliers
- Box cutter + scissors
- Flashlight + batteries
- Duct tape
- Paper towels + trash bags
- All-purpose cleaner + rags
- First aid kit

**Car Emergency Kit:**
- Jumper cables
- Spare tire check + jack
- Roadside assistance # (AAA or insurance)
- Reflective triangle or flares
- Gallon of water
- Blanket
- Phone number of vehicle shipper (if applicable)

**First-Night-in-Oregon Box (ride in the car):**
- Toilet paper + hand soap + shower curtain
- Towels (2 per person)
- Bedding for one bed (sheets, pillow, blanket)
- Coffee + mugs + kettle or French press
- Paper plates, cups, utensils
- Trash bags
- Dog bed + food/water bowls

**Final Walk-Through Checklist (Ohio home):**
- [ ] All rooms, closets, cabinets empty
- [ ] Attic, basement, garage checked
- [ ] Photos/video of each room
- [ ] Meters photographed
- [ ] Windows locked, lights off, thermostat set
- [ ] Keys/fobs/remotes returned
- [ ] Forwarding address left with landlord

**Phone Numbers to Have Handy:**
- Mover dispatch: _______________
- Vehicle shipper: _______________
- Ohio landlord: _______________
- Oregon landlord: _______________
- Current vet: _______________
- New Oregon vet: _______________
- Nearest emergency vet (route + destination): _______________
- Auto insurance: _______________
- Roadside assistance: _______________
- Utility co. (Oregon): _______________

---

## WHAT GOES IN THE CAR vs. THE TRUCK

**In the car with you (never on the truck):**
- All documents (full pouch above)
- Cash, checkbook, wallets
- Prescriptions and medical devices
- Laptops, phones, chargers, external drives, USB with backups
- Jewelry and small valuables
- Family photos/heirlooms you can't replace
- The dog, dog go-bag, dog food (7+ days), and crate
- Day-of comfort bag (clothes, toiletries, meds for 3+ days)
- First-night-in-Oregon box
- Car emergency kit + tool kit
- Snacks, water, cooler
- Any firearms (per legal requirements for transport)
- Plants (movers typically won't take them across state lines anyway)

**On the truck (safe to be unavailable for 3–10 days):**
- All furniture and large appliances
- Boxed books, dishes, kitchenware (beyond day-of basics)
- Bulk of your clothes and shoes
- Decor, art (well-packed), lamps
- Bedding and linens (beyond one set per person)
- Non-essential electronics (TVs, speakers, gaming)
- Garage items, tools, sports gear
- Seasonal items, holiday decor
- Cleaning supplies (non-hazardous only — movers won't take flammables, propane, paint, chemicals, or aerosols)

**Movers will NOT take (dispose of or transport yourself):**
- Propane tanks, gasoline, lighter fluid
- Paint, solvents, cleaning chemicals
- Fireworks, ammunition
- Perishable food
- Plants (most interstate movers)
- Fire extinguishers
- Pool chemicals

**Rule of thumb:** If losing it for 10 days would ruin your week, it rides with you.

# Oregon DMV Guide for New Residents

**Important caveat upfront:** DMV rules, fees, and deadlines change regularly. Everything below is accurate to my knowledge as of early 2026, but **verify every detail on the official Oregon DMV site before you act**. I've flagged the items most likely to shift (fees especially).

Official sources to bookmark now:
- **Oregon DMV (main):** https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/
- **New to Oregon page:** https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/driverid/newtoor.aspx
- **Vehicle registration/title:** https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/vehicle/index.aspx
- **DEQ Vehicle Inspection Program (emissions):** https://www.oregon.gov/deq/aq/programs/pages/vip.aspx
- **DMV office locator and appointments:** https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/offices/index.aspx
- **Real ID in Oregon:** https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/driverid/real_id.aspx
- **Oregon Secretary of State voter registration:** https://sos.oregon.gov/voting/pages/registration.aspx

---

## THE DEADLINE

Oregon requires new residents to get an Oregon driver's license and register their vehicles **within 30 days of establishing residency**. "Establishing residency" generally means taking a job, enrolling kids in school, or renting/buying a home. Confirm the current rule on the "New to Oregon" page above — this is the most commonly cited figure but the exact definition matters.

**Practical advice:** Book your DMV appointment the week you arrive. Walk-ins exist but waits are long, especially in Portland metro.

---

## PART 1: DRIVER'S LICENSE — STEP BY STEP

### Step 1: Decide Standard vs. Real ID

- **Standard Oregon license:** Lets you drive and serves as state ID. Cannot be used to board domestic flights after the federal Real ID enforcement date (currently May 7, 2025; verify current status).
- **Real ID license:** Same driving function plus TSA-acceptable for domestic flights and federal buildings. Requires more documents at the counter.

If you don't have a passport, get the Real ID version. If you do, either works.

### Step 2: Gather Documents

You need **one** from each category below. Bring originals — no photocopies, no laminated docs.

**Proof of identity** (one of):
- U.S. passport or passport card
- Certified birth certificate (not a hospital souvenir copy)
- Permanent Resident Card
- U.S. military ID
- Certificate of Naturalization

**Proof of Social Security Number** (one of):
- Social Security card (unlaminated)
- W-2 with full SSN
- Pay stub with full SSN
- SSA-1099

**Proof of Oregon residency** (two documents for Real ID; one may suffice for standard — verify):
- Oregon lease or mortgage statement
- Utility bill in your name at the Oregon address
- Bank statement mailed to Oregon address
- Oregon voter registration card
- Oregon vehicle registration or title
- Employer letter on letterhead with Oregon address

**Proof of legal name change** (if applicable):
- Marriage certificate
- Divorce decree
- Court order

### Step 3: Surrender Your Ohio License

Oregon will take your Ohio license at the counter and mail it back (punched/invalidated) or destroy it. If you need to keep it for any reason (rare), say so upfront.

### Step 4: Vision Test

Done at the counter. No appointment needed for this piece.

### Step 5: Knowledge Test — Usually Waived

If you have a valid out-of-state license, **Oregon typically waives the written and driving tests**. If your Ohio license is expired more than a year (verify), you may need to test.

### Step 6: Pay the Fee and Get a Temporary

- **Fees (verify current amounts):** Standard 8-year license is roughly $60. Real ID adds about $30. A new ID card (if you don't drive) is around $44.
- You'll leave with a paper interim license. The real card arrives by mail in 2–3 weeks.

### Step 7: Update Voter Registration

Oregon has automatic voter registration through DMV ("Motor Voter"). When you get your license, you're typically registered automatically unless you opt out. Confirm your status at the Secretary of State link above after a few weeks.

---

## PART 2: VEHICLE REGISTRATION — STEP BY STEP

### Step 1: Check for Liens

If you're still paying off either car, **the lienholder holds your title**. You cannot register in Oregon without resolving this. Options:

1. **Call the lienholder and request they send the title to Oregon DMV.** Oregon will register the vehicle with a note that the lien exists. The lienholder may need an Oregon-specific form; Oregon DMV will provide it, or call the lienholder's title department directly. Allow 2–4 weeks.
2. **Provide the lienholder's contact info and your loan account number to Oregon DMV** — they can sometimes coordinate directly.
3. **If you're near payoff**, consider paying off the loan before moving so you hold the title outright. Easiest path.

Start this process **before you leave Ohio** — it's the #1 delay for new Oregon residents.

### Step 2: Do You Need a DEQ Emissions Test?

**Required if you register a vehicle in these areas:**
- **Portland metro:** Multnomah, Washington, and Clackamas counties (and parts of the Portland area generally)
- **Medford area:** Parts of Jackson County near Medford and Central Point

**Not required elsewhere in Oregon** (most of the state).

**Exemptions (verify current rules):**
- Brand new vehicles (typically first few model years)
- Fully electric vehicles
- Motorcycles
- Vehicles older than a certain year (historically pre-1975, verify)

**How it works:**
- Find a DEQ station: https://www.oregon.gov/deq/aq/programs/pages/vip.aspx
- Current fee is approximately **$25** (Portland area) or **$21** (Medford) — verify.
- No appointment needed at most stations, but weekday mornings are fastest.
- Bring your current (Ohio) registration.
- You'll get a Vehicle Inspection Report. Pass = you can register. Fail = you must repair and retest.
- DEQ offers a free "DEQ Too" online self-service option for newer OBD-II vehicles in some cases. Check the site.

**Timing:** Do this **before** your DMV appointment to register. Some people do DMV first and emissions after; cleaner to do emissions first and bring the pass certificate to DMV.

### Step 3: VIN Inspection

Oregon requires a **VIN verification** for out-of-state vehicles being titled in Oregon for the first time. This confirms the VIN on the car matches your documents.

- Done at any Oregon DMV office — usually at the time of your registration appointment.
- The DMV employee walks out to your car and checks the VIN plate.
- Bring the car to your appointment. No separate trip needed.
- **Free** when done as part of titling.

### Step 4: Gather Vehicle Documents

- **Title** (original, or confirmation lienholder is sending it)
- **Current Ohio registration**
- **Oregon driver's license** (get this first, same day is fine)
- **Proof of Oregon auto insurance** (minimum liability: 25/50/20 property damage plus PIP and uninsured motorist — verify current minimums)
- **Odometer reading** (DMV form at the counter, or bring your own from your Ohio title transfer)
- **DEQ passing certificate** if required
- **Lienholder information** if applicable (name, address, account number)
- **Vehicle Title Application** (DMV form 735-226, available on the site to pre-fill)

### Step 5: Fees — What to Expect

**Verify all of these on the DMV fee page; they change.** Rough current estimates:

| Fee | Approximate Cost |
|---|---|
| Title transfer | $101 |
| Registration (2-year, passenger car) | $126–$156 depending on vehicle MPG |
| Registration (electric vehicle, 2-year) | $306 |
| Plate fee | Included |
| VIN inspection | Included with title |
| DEQ emissions (Portland metro) | ~$25 |
| DEQ emissions (Medford) | ~$21 |

**Important Oregon quirk:** Registration fees are **tiered by fuel economy**. Higher-MPG and electric vehicles pay more (EVs pay significantly more to offset lost gas tax revenue). Check your vehicle's fee at the DMV site before you go.

**Portland metro surcharge:** Vehicles registered in the Portland metro area pay an additional county fee for transportation funding. Expect roughly $56 extra for 2 years in Multnomah County, with Washington and Clackamas at slightly lower amounts. Verify current rates.

### Step 6: Get Plates and Registration

- You get Oregon plates at the counter. Install them on the car before leaving the lot.
- Return/destroy your Ohio plates. Ohio BMV asks you to surrender them or follow their cancellation process — check https://bmv.ohio.gov/.
- Your new title arrives by mail in 4–8 weeks. If there's a lien, the title goes to the lienholder.

### Step 7: Cancel Ohio Registration and Insurance

- Cancel Ohio registration via the Ohio BMV once Oregon registration is complete.
- Transfer your auto insurance policy to Oregon. **Do not let coverage lapse at any point.** Call your insurer the week before you move and set the switchover date.

---

## COUNTY DIFFERENCES: PORTLAND METRO vs. RURAL

### Portland Metro (Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas)
- **Emissions test required.**
- Transportation surcharge added to registration.
- DMV offices are busier; **book appointments 3–6 weeks out**. Walk-ins may wait 2–4 hours.
- Try smaller-area offices (Gresham, Hillsboro, Oregon City) over downtown Portland for shorter waits.
- Dog licensing done through your county: Multnomah County Animal Services, Washington County, or Clackamas County Dog Services. Required and enforced.

### Medford Area (parts of Jackson County)
- **Emissions test required** in the Medford/Central Point boundary; **not required** in outlying Jackson County areas.
- Verify your specific address at the DEQ site.

### Rural Oregon (everywhere else)
- **No emissions test required.**
- No county transportation surcharge.
- DMV offices much faster; often same-day walk-in service.
- Dog licensing still required but through your county.

**Strategy tip:** If you're moving somewhere near a county line, your registration county is based on your residence address, not where you register. You can drive to any DMV office in the state to do the transaction, but your fees are based on where you live.

---

## RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE (First Week in Oregon)

1. **Day 1–2:** Settle in, confirm residency address, gather documents.
2. **Day 2:** Book DMV appointment (go to the appointment scheduler link above). Soonest available may be 1–3 weeks out in metro, same-week in rural.
3. **Day 3:** Call lienholder(s) if you have a car loan. Start title transfer process.
4. **Day 3–5:** Transfer auto insurance to Oregon address.
5. **Before DMV appointment:** Get DEQ emissions test if required.

## 2. MULTNOMAH COUNTY ADDENDUM

*For Portland and inner-metro residents.*

---

**MULTNOMAH COUNTY — DMV & EMISSIONS QUICK REFERENCE**

**EMISSIONS (DEQ) — REQUIRED**

- Cost: **~$25 per vehicle** (verify current)
- No appointment needed; weekday mornings fastest
- Bring: current Ohio registration + payment
- Pass certificate valid for registration

**DEQ stations serving Multnomah County:**
- **Portland NE** — 1230 NE 61st Ave, Portland
- **Portland SE** — 9350 SE Division St, Portland
- **Gresham** — 1800 SW Royal Woodlands Pkwy area (verify current address)
- **Scappoose** (overflow option) — a bit farther, often shorter lines
- Full station list: https://www.oregon.gov/deq/aq/programs/pages/vip-stations.aspx
- **DEQ Too** online self-service (eligible OBD-II vehicles): https://www.deqtoo.org

**COUNTY SURCHARGE**

Multnomah County vehicles pay an additional registration surcharge on top of state fees:
- **~$56 per vehicle for 2-year registration** (verify current rate)
- Funds regional transportation (Metro area)
- Automatically added at DMV; no separate payment

**Total 2-year registration in Multnomah (passenger car):** roughly **$180–$215** depending on MPG, plus ~$101 title transfer.

**FASTEST DMV OFFICES (Multnomah area)**

In order of typical wait times — fastest first:

1. **Gresham DMV** — Usually shortest metro wait; often 1–2 weeks out for appointment
2. **Oregon City DMV** (Clackamas County, 20 min south) — Fast, often same-week
3. **Hillsboro DMV** (Washington County, 25 min west) — Fast, often same-week
4. **Portland (SE 122nd)** — Moderate wait, 2–3 weeks out
5. **Portland Downtown / NE Portland** — Longest waits, 4–6 weeks out

**Strategy:** You can register at any Oregon DMV regardless of where you live. Fees are based on your home address, not the office. Drive to Gresham or Oregon City to save weeks.

**APPOINTMENT BOOKING**
- Online: https://www.oregon.gov/odot/dmv/pages/offices/index.aspx
- Book both license + vehicle reg in same appointment slot if possible
- Separate appointments per person if both getting licenses

**DOG LICENSE — MULTNOMAH**
- Required within **30 days** of residency
- Multnomah County Animal Services: https://www.multco.us/animal-services
- ~$18–$35 depending on spay/neuter status
- Rabies certificate required
- Can register online

## 1. UTILITIES TIMELINE

## 2. PORTLAND METRO PROVIDER LIST

### Electric
Service area determines provider — you don't choose.

- **Portland General Electric (PGE)** — serves most of Portland, Beaverton, Tualatin, parts of Clackamas
  - https://portlandgeneral.com | (503) 228-6322
  - Lead time: 2–3 business days
  - Deposit: usually waived with good credit; $100–$300 otherwise

- **Pacific Power** — serves outer Washington County, parts of Clackamas, rural areas
  - https://pacificpower.net | (888) 221-7070
  - Lead time: 2–3 business days
  - Deposit: usually waived with good credit; $150–$300 otherwise

### Natural Gas
- **NW Natural** — serves nearly all of Portland metro
  - https://nwnatural.com | (800) 422-4012
  - Lead time: 3–5 business days (longer if pilot light needs lighting)
  - Deposit: usually waived; ~$100 if required
  - **Important:** If service is off, a technician must come to relight pilots. Schedule during business hours.

### Water / Sewer / Trash
Varies by city — municipal, not private. Usually combined on one bill.

- **City of Portland Water Bureau** — https://portland.gov/water | (503) 823-7770
  - Water + sewer billed together; trash separate (see below)
  - Auto-start when you register as new resident
- **Tualatin Valley Water District** (Beaverton, Hillsboro, Tigard area) — https://tvwd.org | (503) 848-3000
- **Clackamas River Water** — https://crwater.com | (503) 722-9220

### Trash & Recycling
- **Portland:** Choose a franchise hauler by address — enter address at https://portland.gov/bps/garbage-recycling to see your required hauler
- **Washington County / Hillsboro area:** Varies by city, often Pride Disposal or Waste Management
- **Clackamas County:** Varies — Republic Services, Waste Management, or local haulers
- **Recology** operates in parts of outer metro and Clark County WA, not Portland proper (common misconception)
- Lead time: 1–2 business days
- Deposit: usually none

### Internet (ISPs)
**Book 2–3 weeks ahead minimum.** Install slots fill fast.

- **Ziply Fiber** — Fastest growing in metro; fiber in most new areas
  - https://ziply.com | (866) 699-4759
  - Lead time: 1–3 weeks
  - Deposit: usually none; equipment fee if not using own router

- **Xfinity (Comcast)** — Widest coverage; cable
  - https://xfinity.com | (800) 934-6489
  - Lead time: 1–2 weeks; self-install kits same-week
  - Deposit: usually none with autopay

- **CenturyLink / Quantum Fiber** — DSL + fiber in some areas
  - https://centurylink.com | (800) 244-1111
  - Lead time: 1–3 weeks

- **T-Mobile Home Internet / Verizon 5G Home** — No install needed
  - Ship-to-door, self-setup same day
  - Good backup if ISP install delayed

### Cable / TV
Most households cut cable — skip and use streaming. If needed, bundled through Xfinity or Ziply.

### Electricity Note
Oregon has deregulated some electric options but residential customers in the Portland metro are generally stuck with PGE or Pacific Power by service area. Shop for a different provider only if you're in a transitional service area.
